pageProps.review: Bernard Werber's novel The Sixth Sleep 2 stands out for its fresh subject matter and giant imagination, but it's a work that gives a feeling of a 'dragon's head and a snake's tail' due to its convenient setup and repeated narrative in the latter half.

## Review
I am surprised by the freshness of the subject matter in Bernard's works, but left with disappointment at the too grandiose and forced conclusions.  
<mark>A giant imagination with an anticlimactic ending</mark>
Compared to the freshness of volume 1, the development of volume 2 leaves something to be desired.  
The mystery and tension carefully built up were solved too easily with the appearance of a too convenient setup.  
The narrative structure also repeats too much, which gives a sense of déjà vu.
